newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats hopeful of wage agreement with NUM.
newsitem.headline: Amplats hopeful of wage agreement with NUM.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp (Amplats) said on Tuesday it was hopeful of settling wage negotiations with the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) in arbitration talks due to begin soon.
"We are going to the CCMA (Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration) on the 12th or 13th of this month," Amplats operations director Brian Beamish told a news briefing.
"I'm hoping that with the CCMA we'll get to some sort of agreement which will satisfy both parties. I'm fairly hopeful that we're going to get to a pretty good settlement."

Beamish said the company had agreed a straight six percent increase plus an additional percentage for working on public holidays with other unions but was in stalemate with the NUM -- the most widely represented union across its three mines.

The company earlier unveiled lower annual net earnings which it blamed on a strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd in May and higher operating costs at Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd and Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd.
Its earnings per share for the year to June 30 fell from 190.3 cents to 162.8 cents.
